basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'His itaque transactis, factus est sermo Domini ad Abram per visionem, dicens: Noli'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: His itaque transactis, factus est sermo Domini ad Abram per visionem, dicens: Noli timere, Abram, ego protector tuus sum et merces tua magna nimis. Benedictionem quam a sacerdote Melchisedech perceperat Abraham, hanc per se Dominus ipse confirmat. Dixerat quippe sacerdos: Et benedictus Deus excelsus, quo protegente hostes in manibus tuis sunt (Gen. XIV, 20). Dicit Dominus: Ego protector tuus sum. Dixerat sacerdos: Benedictus Deus excelsus. Dicit ipse Deus: Et merces tua magna nimis. Mercedem autem dicit, non tantum dilectionis, quam fratri in angustia posito exhibuerat; sed et totius dilectionis, qua ipsi Domino ex quo patriam parentesque deseruerat, integro ex corde servierat.
